idea.title: Mistakenly seeking solitude
idea.summary: Epley and Schroeder's 2014 commuter study: people expected a quiet ride alone to be better, but those asked to talk to a stranger enjoyed it more. Opens as a question so the viewer guesses first.
hookOptions: Would you talk to a stranger on the train?
Commuters said they'd hate talking to a stranger
Silence on the train is overrated
I'd rather ride alone, said everyone
sources: Epley, N. & Schroeder, J. (2014). Mistakenly seeking solitude. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General. Participants were Chicago-area train and bus commuters.
Finding: commuters predicted a more positive experience in solitude, but those asked to connect with a stranger reported a more positive experience than those who kept to themselves.

scenes.question: Talk to a stranger on the train?
scenes.say: Commuters said they'd hate talking to a stranger.
So psychologists Nicholas Epley and Juliana Schroeder asked commuters to predict their ride.
They expected silence to win, but some were told to talk anyway.
And the talkers enjoyed their ride more than the quiet ones.

scenes.name: Breezy Moose
scenes.label: Your guess, tested
scenes.say: So if you'd rather stay quiet, test that guess on someone new.
You might like it more than you think.
